game: NE @ TB Week 10 2025, kickoff 2025-11-09 13:00 ET, Raymond James outdoor

script.base: Closing line is TB -2.5 with a 48.5 total, so the book has a one-score home win and implied totals TB 25.5 / NE 23.0, not a blowout. TB, with Chris Godwin out and Mike Evans at 4 targets for 0 yards over weeks 6-8, leans on Emeka Egbuka (25 targets, 117 yards, 320 air) and Cade Otton (20 targets, 156 yards) while Rachaad White (40 carries, 138 yards) runs with Bucky Irving out and Sean Tucker mixing in (19/71). NE answers in a competitive script: Drake Maye has been the blitz-beater (EPA/db 0.44 vs blitz, 0.21 vs none) against Tampa's 38% blitz, the carries split among Rhamondre Stevenson (32/122), TreVeyon Henderson (26/135) and Maye (17/138), and the pass game goes through Stefon Diggs (16 targets) with Demario Douglas the efficiency spike (10 targets, 161 yards, 172 air).
script.flip1: TB leads by two scores at half, clocks it with White and Tucker, and NE's backfield rush lines stall while Maye throws to catch up — Douglas, Diggs and Hunter Henry stay live, White's rush holds, and a NE team-total under becomes the risk.
script.flip2: NE's ground game (Henderson 5.2 YPC plus Maye's 138 rush yards in weeks 7-9) controls the clock, holds TB under 25.5, and a Luke Goedeke or Luke Haggard scratch turns Baker Mayfield's protection bad — Otton can still live on quick throws, but Egbuka's 320 air yards die and the 48.5 total drifts under.

injury_fallout: Known pre-kick from the nflverse injury report, not from inactives (those lock ~90 minutes before kick and are not in the pack). TB: Bucky Irving out (foot) locks White as the lead back and Tucker as the change-of-pace, not a new bellcow; Chris Godwin Jr. out (fibula) pushes targets to Egbuka, Otton, Sterling Shepard and Tez Johnson, but Evans has not absorbed them (4 targets, 0 yards, 97 air in weeks 6-8); Haason Reddick out (ankle) and Markees Watts out (hand) thin the TB front, which helps Maye's time to throw; Goedeke (foot) and Haggard (shoulder) are questionable tackles, so if both sit TB pressure rate and rushing efficiency get worse and quick throws to Otton/White rise. NE: Stevenson questionable (toe) — if he sits or is snap-limited, Henderson is next man up, but that is not confirmed; Kayshon Boutte questionable (hamstring) — if he sits, Diggs, Douglas, Mack Hollins and Henry absorb a share that was 8 targets / 130 yards / 174 air in weeks 7-9; Christian Elliss questionable (hip) — if he sits, TB's TE/RB receiving (Otton, White) faces a backup linebacker. No rep-limit numbers are in the pack.

matchup.shell: No MOFO/MOFC or man/zone charting in the pack, so shell is unknown. Infer only from location splits: TB middle is the leak (9.29 YPA on 48 attempts) versus left 5.93 (105) and right 7.71 (124); NE is flatter, left 7.8 (120), middle 7.18 (62), right 7.19 (105).
matchup.pressure: TB blitzes 38% and NE is better when blitzed (EPA/db 0.44 vs 0.21 unblitzed), so Tampa's pressure plan does not scare Maye; Reddick out further softens the four-man rush. NE blitzes only 24%, and Mayfield is worse when blitzed (EPA/db -0.22) than in base (0.30), so the likely NE plan is the one Mayfield handles.
matchup.bleeds: TB bleeds the middle (9.29 YPA) and has allowed 26 passes of 20+ for 302 yards in 8 games; rush defense is 3.95 YPC with 16 runs of 10+. NE rush defense is the stronger unit at 3.69 YPC and only 14 runs of 10+ in 9 games, while the pass defense has allowed more explosives (31 of 20+ for 307 yards), with the left side the relative soft spot at 7.8 YPA.
matchup.overlap: Douglas, as the recent NE efficiency/slot-type option (172 air yards, 161 yards on 10 targets), overlaps the TB middle leak and the blitz Maye has beaten. Otton overlaps the Godwin absence and NE's low blitz rate, not a giant YPA hole. White's rush overlaps a NE strength (3.69 YPC), so that is not the core edge.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both overs lost. Douglas finished under 17.5 because the 71/44/100 games were explosives against softer shells, TB's middle 9.29 YPA is only 48 attempts of noise, and Maye ran (17 carries, 138 yards in weeks 7-9) while Diggs, Hollins and Henry took the throws — the 17 already in his last4 is the real role and 17.5 is a depth-receiver median for a reason. Otton finished under 40.5 because the 40-yard game is the floor, Evans was never hurt and turned those 97 empty air yards into a 50-plus day once Godwin's targets came open, and Goedeke plus Haggard both sat so Mayfield's bad blitz EPA showed up even against a 24% blitz. That counter is strong enough to keep Otton a lean and to flag the missing no-vig, but it is not stronger than Douglas's three-game 161-yard role, so Douglas stays.
